sentences.en: Hi, Anna.

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: I'm good.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: Tell me what the show is this week.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲这周的节目是什么吧。

sentences.en: So I have a question for you.
sentences.zh: 所以我有个问题想问你。

sentences.en: Do you ever find yourself wondering about people that are close to you?
sentences.zh: 你有没有发现自己会去揣测那些与你亲近的人？

sentences.en: Do you ever find yourself wondering, are you mad at me?
sentences.zh: 你有没有发现自己会想：你是在生我的气吗？

sentences.en: Literally every day, unfortunately.

sentences.en: Multiple times a day.
sentences.zh: 一天好几次。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, then this is the episode for you.
sentences.zh: 那这就是为你量身打造的一期节目。

sentences.en: This week, I talked to a therapist named Meg Josephson, who helped me understand where that question comes from, why we ask it, and maybe how to stop.
sentences.zh: 本周，我采访了一位名叫梅格·约瑟夫森的治疗师，她帮我理解了那个问题从何而来，我们为什么会这样问，以及或许该如何停止。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I'm so excited for this.
sentences.zh: 我太期待这个了。

sentences.en: I'm going to be sending this to four or five of my friends.
sentences.zh: 我要把这期节目发给我四五个朋友。

sentences.en: Good, good.
sentences.zh: 很好，很好。

sentences.en: Everyone, Anna Martin, and this week's episode of Modern Love.

sentences.zh: 你上次坠入爱河了吗？

sentences.zh: 我感受到了爱。

sentences.zh: 而我爱你胜过一切。

sentences.zh: 这就是爱。

sentences.en: Love.

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Anna Martin.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是安娜·马丁。

sentences.en: This is Modern Love.
sentences.zh: 这里是《现代爱情》。

sentences.en: Every week, we bring you stories about all the messiness of relating to other people.
sentences.zh: 每周，我们都会为你带来关于人际交往中种种混乱与纠葛的故事。

sentences.en: Any time my boss would slack me, can we chat or do you have a sec?
sentences.zh: 每当我的老板在工作软件上发消息问我：我们能聊聊吗，或者你有空吗？

sentences.en: Immediate sinking feeling in my stomach.
sentences.zh: 我的胃里立刻有一种往下沉的感觉。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: It's time.
sentences.zh: 时候到了。

sentences.en: I'm getting fired.
sentences.zh: 我要被解雇了。

sentences.en: I've done something horribly wrong, and I'm about to have it.
sentences.zh: 我做了什么十恶不赦的错事，而这就要被发现了。

sentences.en: My guest today is therapist and author Meg Josephson.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是治疗师兼作家梅格·约瑟夫森。

sentences.en: Meg has a new book coming out called Are You Mad at Me?
sentences.zh: 梅格有一本新书即将出版，书名叫《你是在生我的气吗？》

sentences.en: It's a look at this nagging, sneaking suspicion that you've done something wrong, that you're letting everyone down.
sentences.zh: 这本书探讨了那种挥之不去、鬼祟的怀疑，觉得你做错了什么，觉得你让所有人失望了。

sentences.en: Just an immediate assumption that there is an inherent flaw within ourselves.
sentences.zh: 这是一种直接的假设，认为我们自身存在着某种固有的缺陷。

sentences.en: Am I in trouble?
sentences.zh: 我是不是惹麻烦了？

sentences.en: Is something wrong with me?
sentences.zh: 我有什么问题吗？

sentences.en: Am I bad?
sentences.zh: 我是个坏人吗？

sentences.en: Am I secretly bad?
sentences.zh: 我暗地里是个坏人吗？

sentences.en: And it's just a matter of time before everyone finds out.
sentences.zh: 而且这只是时间问题，直到所有人都发现这一点。

sentences.en: Meg grew up with that question.
sentences.zh: 梅格就是在那种质问中长大的。

sentences.en: Are you mad at me?
sentences.zh: 你是在生我的气吗？

sentences.en: Always at the front of her mind.
sentences.zh: 永远占据在她脑海的最前沿。

sentences.en: She was always on the lookout, trying to keep her dad, in particular, from getting angry.
sentences.zh: 她总是小心翼翼，试图阻止她的父亲，尤其是他生气。

sentences.en: Every hour was so different.
sentences.zh: 每一个小时都大不相同。

sentences.en: Let me go downstairs and see what mood he's in, and that will determine my strategy for the next hour.
sentences.zh: 让我下楼去看看他是什么心情，这决定了我接下来一小时的应对策略。

sentences.en: And this fear of authority was really big.
sentences.zh: 这种对权威的恐惧非常强烈。

sentences.en: Like, growing up, it was fear of my dad, but now it was fear of my boss.
sentences.zh: 比如，在成长过程中，是对父亲的恐惧，而现在是对老板的恐惧。

sentences.en: Meg spent years doing this, trying to manage other people's reactions, trying to please them, trying to keep the peace.
sentences.zh: 梅格花了好几年做这件事，试图掌控他人的反应，试图取悦他们，试图维持和平。

sentences.en: It wasn't until she was an adult that she realized what she was doing wasn't helping her.
sentences.zh: 直到她长大成人，她才意识到她做的事对她毫无帮助。

sentences.en: And what she was doing had a name.
sentences.zh: 而且她所做的事情有一个名字。

sentences.en: Fawning.
sentences.zh: 讨好。

sentences.en: Today, Meg Josephson tells us what it took to stop worrying about whether everyone was mad at her, and how understanding what happened in her childhood helped her make that change.
sentences.zh: 今天，梅格·约瑟夫森将告诉我们，她花了多大努力才不再担心所有人是否都在生她的气，以及理解童年发生的事情是如何帮助她做出这种改变的。

sentences.en: Plus, she reads a Modern Love essay about a woman who gets a peek at what her parents could have been, and how it helps her come to terms with the parents she actually has.
sentences.zh: 此外，她还朗读了一篇《现代爱情》的散文，讲述了一个女人如何一窥她父母本可能成为的样子，以及这如何帮助她与实际拥有的父母达成和解。

sentences.en: Meg Josephson, welcome to Modern Love.
sentences.zh: 梅格·约瑟夫森，欢迎来到《现代爱情》。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: First, I want to say, I almost cannot express how deeply I relate to the title of your book.
sentences.zh: 首先，我想说，我几乎无法表达我对你书名的共鸣有多深。

sentences.en: It's called, Are You Mad at Me?
sentences.zh: 它叫《你是在生我的气吗？》

sentences.en: This is a question I find I ask myself in so many relationships, in different contexts.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己在很多关系中、在不同的语境下都会问自己这个问题。

sentences.en: Some of them, very serious, like,
sentences.zh: 其中一些非常严肃，比如，

sentences.en: Oh my gosh, is my mom mad at me for some fundamental reason?
sentences.zh: 天哪，我妈是不是因为什么根本原因在生我的气？

sentences.en: But then also, I feel like, you know, after, for example, a recent night out with my friends,
sentences.zh: 但随后，我也觉得，你知道的，比如在最近和朋友们的一晚外出之后，

sentences.en: the morning after, I find myself texting, and I hope this is kind of a universal experience, but I already think it is.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上，我发现自己发着短信，我希望这是一种普遍的体验，但我已经觉得它是了。

sentences.en: Yes, with my friend after being like, was I weird?
sentences.zh: 是的，跟朋友发消息说，我很奇怪吗？

sentences.en: Maybe that joke was a little, was I speaking too loud?
sentences.zh: 也许那个笑话有点……我说话声音是不是太大了？

sentences.en: Sometimes my volume control goes out the window.
sentences.zh: 有时候我对音量的控制完全失控了。

sentences.en: I mean, at the heart of that question, I wasn't saying, are you mad at me, or are they mad at me?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在这个问题的核心，我并不是在问你是在生我的气，或者他们在生我的气吗？

sentences.en: But that's what I was asking, right?
sentences.zh: 但那就是我在问的，对吧？

sentences.en: I was seeking confirmation from someone that I wasn't fundamentally, if not bad, then like, very annoying.
sentences.zh: 我在向某人寻求确认，确认我本质上如果不算坏的话，至少也不是非常烦人。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And is how I'm behaving, is how I'm acting satisfying to you?
sentences.zh: 并且我的表现、我的行为对你来说是令人满意的吗？

sentences.en: Do you approve of it?
sentences.zh: 你赞同吗？

sentences.en: Do you like it?
sentences.zh: 你喜欢吗？

sentences.en: Are people viewing me in a way that I'm not aware of, that I need to correct my behavior so that I can be approved of once again?
sentences.zh: 大家看我的方式是不是我没有意识到、需要我去纠正行为以便能再次获得认可的？

sentences.en: Tell me about when you're asking these questions about yourself, what are some other feelings that are associated with this, with this cluster of questions,
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲，当你这样质问自己时，还有哪些其他的情绪与这一类问题、

sentences.en: the are you mad at me universe of questions?
sentences.zh: 这一系列“你是在生我的气吗”的宇宙相关联？

sentences.en: Shame is a big one as, as the, I think the, the deepest, but I think other emotions
sentences.zh: 羞耻感是一个很大的情绪，作为我觉得最深层的情绪，但我认为其他情绪

sentences.en: and emotions that someone, a fawner, which we can talk about what that means, but someone who relates to this question of are you mad at me,
sentences.zh: 那些倾向于讨好的人的情绪——我们可以讨论这意味着什么——但那些对“你是在生我的气吗”这个问题感同身受的人，

sentences.en: anger and resentment are really big ones in that we don't allow ourselves to feel them.
sentences.zh: 愤怒和怨恨是非常大的情绪，因为我们不允许自己去感受它们。

sentences.en: And the slight smile when you said that, unpack that smile for me.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说这话时带着一丝微笑，为我解构一下那个微笑吧。

sentences.en: Well, with, with anger, many of us usually in childhood were taught, I can't feel anger.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对于愤怒，我们很多人通常在童年就被教导，我不能感受愤怒。

sentences.en: My, my parents, my caregivers can feel anger and maybe they felt that anger in really extreme ways, whether it was through yelling and rage or silent treatment,
sentences.zh: 我的父母、我的照顾者可以感受愤怒，也许他们以非常极端的方式表达了这种愤怒，无论是通过大喊大叫和暴怒还是冷暴力，

sentences.en: but it was not dealt with in a regulated, safe and healthy way.
sentences.zh: 但它并没有以一种受控、安全和健康的方式处理。

sentences.en: So we learn anger is scary.
sentences.zh: 所以我们学会了愤怒是可怕的。

sentences.en: Anger means love is taken away from me.
sentences.zh: 愤怒意味着爱被从我身边夺走了。

sentences.en: And when we felt anger growing up, a lot of us were told you're being dramatic or get over it.
sentences.zh: 当我们长大后感到愤怒时，很多人被告知你太戏剧化了或者看开点。

sentences.en: We were taught to shove it down, but we also learn, I keep the peace the moSt.
sentences.zh: 我们被教导将它压抑下去，但我们也明白，当我表现得随和、积极、乐于挑选和精选我们的情绪时，

sentences.en: When I'm easy and positive and happy to select and curate our emotions.
sentences.zh: 我能最好地维持和平。

sentences.en: However, those emotions don't go anywhere.
sentences.zh: 然而，那些情绪并没有消失。

sentences.en: They're still there.
sentences.zh: 它们依然在那里。

sentences.en: They just get shoved down into our bodies.
sentences.zh: 它们只是被压抑进我们的身体里。

sentences.en: And when we shove that anger down, when we shove those needs down again and again, it festers into resentment.
sentences.zh: 而当我们一次又一次地压抑这种愤怒，当我们一次又一次地压抑那些需求时，它就会恶化成怨恨。

sentences.en: And whenever someone's feeling resentful, it's always a sign of, okay, let's, let's tune in a little bit.
sentences.zh: 每当有人感到怨恨时，这总是一个信号，好吧，让我们稍微调整一下。

sentences.en: And what's happening here?
sentences.zh: 这里到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: What needs have to be addressed?
sentences.zh: 有什么需求需要被满足？

sentences.en: Tell me more about this sort of, you mentioned fawning.
sentences.zh: 再跟我多讲讲这种，你提到的讨好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: F-A-W-N.
sentences.zh: F-A-W-N.

sentences.en: I feel the need to spell it out loud, but fawning, the fawn response.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有必要把它说清楚，但讨好，讨好反应。

sentences.en: And you mentioned a bit like making ourselves more palatable to people, squishing our emotions down to be pleasing.
sentences.zh: 你提到了有点像让我们自己对别人来说更容易接受，把我们的情绪压下去以求讨好。

sentences.en: Tell me more about what the fawn response is and how it relates to this question of, are you mad at me?
sentences.zh: 多跟我讲讲什么是讨好反应，以及它与“你是在生我的气吗”这个问题有什么关系。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So our body has four responses to a threat, whether or not that threat is real or perceived.
sentences.zh: 所以面对威胁，无论这种威胁是真实存在的还是我们感觉到的，我们的身体有四种反应。

sentences.en: So it doesn't have to be in front of us.
sentences.zh: 所以它不一定非得在我们的眼前。

sentences.en: It could just be, oh, my boss is being kind of standoffish to me.
sentences.zh: 它可能只是，哦，我的老板对我有点冷淡疏离。

sentences.en: That feels threatening, even though there's not a line in front of you.
sentences.zh: 这感觉很有威胁性，尽管你面前并没有一条警戒线。

sentences.en: We have fight or flight, which a lot of us may be familiar with, freeze.
sentences.zh: 我们有战斗或逃跑，很多人可能很熟悉，还有僵住。

sentences.en: And the fourth one is the fawn response.
sentences.zh: 第四种就是讨好反应。

sentences.en: And the fawn response is about appeasing the threat, trying to be liked by it, satisfying it, trying to impress it or prove yourself to it.
sentences.zh: 而讨好反应就是安抚威胁，试图博得它的好感，满足它，试图给它留下深刻印象或向它证明你自己。

sentences.en: Really, the fawn response says, my safety comes from pleasing you.
sentences.zh: 实际上，讨好反应的意思是，我的安全来自于取悦你。

sentences.en: And I can't feel regulated until you're regulated.
sentences.zh: 在你情绪平复之前，我的情绪无法平静。

sentences.en: This is not a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 这不是一件坏事。

sentences.en: It's a protective thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一种保护机制。

sentences.en: And it's an unconscious survival mechanism.
sentences.zh: 这是一个无意识的生存机制。

sentences.en: And sometimes we need it.
sentences.zh: 有时我们需要它。

sentences.en: We need a paycheck.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一份薪水。

sentences.en: Sometimes we need to fawn with our boss.
sentences.zh: 有时我们需要对老板进行讨好。

sentences.en: Sometimes in society, while surviving in oppressive systems, we have to fawn in order to survive.
sentences.zh: 有时在社会中，为了在压迫性的体制中生存，我们必须通过讨好来活下去。

sentences.en: But when we're doing it as our default way of being, when we're in a fawn response, when we don't need it, when we're actually safe, that's where it leads to burnout, exhaustion,
sentences.zh: 但当我们将它作为我们默认的生存方式，当我们处于讨好反应中，而我们并不需要它、我们实际上很安全时，这就会导致职业倦怠、精疲力竭、

sentences.en: overthinking, are they mad at me?
sentences.zh: 过度思考：他们是在生我的气吗？

sentences.en: Overthinking social interactions and avoiding conflict and inability to have hard conversations because we just, we don't want people thinking we disagree with them.
sentences.zh: 过度思考社交互动，回避冲突，无法进行艰难的对话，因为我们只是、我们不想让别人觉得我们不同意他们的看法。

sentences.en: And a really big consequence or maybe results is a better word of a chronic fawn response is feeling like we don't know who we are.
sentences.zh: 而长期讨好反应的一个非常大的后果，或者说结果用这个词更好，就是觉得自己不知道自己是谁。

sentences.en: I want to break in because you have this example from your book about the sort of, what's the word?
sentences.zh: 我想打断一下，因为你书里有一个例子，关于那种，怎么说呢？

sentences.en: Maybe like how thoroughly we can internalize this fawning response and this sort of need to placate other people that we can lose ourselves, as you say, right?
sentences.zh: 也许就像我们可以多么彻底地将这种讨好反应内化，以及那种迎合他人的需求，以至于正如你所说，我们会迷失自我？

sentences.en: There's this example where I think you're in a bed, bath, and beyond.
sentences.zh: 有一个例子，我想你当时是在家居乐（Bed Bath & Beyond）。

sentences.en: Did I make that up?
sentences.zh: 是我编造的吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay, yes.
sentences.zh: 好的，是的。

sentences.en: You are in a bed, bath, and beyond.
sentences.zh: 你置身于家居乐购物中心中。

sentences.en: Tell me that story about the towels.
sentences.zh: 给我讲讲那个关于毛巾的故事。

sentences.en: Well, maybe some background might be helpful.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许了解一些背景会有所帮助。

sentences.en: I grew up in a home that was quite volatile and there was a lot of rage from my dad.
sentences.zh: 我在一个相当动荡的家庭中长大，我父亲经常大发雷霆。

sentences.en: And because of that, I think as my mom's way of coping, a lot of emotional absence for her.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，我想我妈妈的应对方式是，情感上非常缺席。

sentences.en: I think her way of coping was kind of through dissociation and freezing and that's how she could make sense of it.
sentences.zh: 我想她是通过解离和呆滞来应对的，这就是她能理解这一切的方式。

sentences.en: And my dad also struggled with addiction as well.
sentences.zh: 而且我父亲也饱受毒瘾困扰。

sentences.en: So there was just a lot going on.
sentences.zh: 所以当时情况真的很复杂。

sentences.en: So Are You Mad at Me was always in my mind.
sentences.zh: 因此，“你生我的气吗”这个问题总是萦绕在我脑海中。

sentences.en: You know, that was really helpful for me growing up.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这对我成长真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: And then when I left, when I moved out, I moved to New York City and I was looking for towels for my 4x4 apartment.
sentences.zh: 后来当我离开家，搬到纽约市时，我正在为我的四乘四英尺的小公寓寻找毛巾。

sentences.en: We called it a shoebox in these parts.
sentences.zh: 我们在当地把这叫做鞋盒。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 对，完全是这样。

sentences.en: I'm in the aisle.
sentences.zh: 我在过道里。

sentences.en: I'm looking for towels.
sentences.zh: 我在找毛巾。

sentences.en: And there's all these colors in front of me.
sentences.zh: 我面前有各种各样的颜色。

sentences.en: And I remember, and this is maybe the first instance where I'm, not the first, but I'm in an instance where I'm like, okay, I'm choosing this for myself.
sentences.zh: 我记得，这可能是我第一次……也不是第一次，但这是我第一次遇到这样的情况：好吧，我在为自己做选择。

sentences.en: And I had no, I just, my first thought was, I don't even, I don't know what my favorite color is.
sentences.zh: 我当时完全……我的第一反应是，我甚至……我不知道我最喜欢的颜色是什么。

sentences.en: How did that thought come to you?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么产生这种想法的？

sentences.en: It's like you were picking one up and you were like, do I like this?
sentences.zh: 就像你拿起一条毛巾，然后心想：我喜欢这个吗？

sentences.en: I was thinking, well, my, the second thought that followed that was, let me, let me go on Instagram and see what other people are doing.
sentences.zh: 我在想，紧接着第二个想法是：让我去Instagram上看看别人都在用什么。

sentences.en: Or let me see what's, what's trendy right now.
sentences.zh: 或者让我看看现在流行什么。

sentences.en: And just this, this immediate shame of, who, who am I?
sentences.zh: 紧接着涌起一种羞耻感：我是谁？

sentences.en: And am I just copying people's personalities?
sentences.zh: 我是不是只是在模仿别人的个性？

sentences.en: Am I just a medley of other people's personalities and preferences?
sentences.zh: 我难道只是别人个性和偏好的大杂烩吗？

sentences.en: And what do I want?
sentences.zh: 我到底想要什么？

sentences.en: What do I like?
sentences.zh: 我喜欢什么？

sentences.en: What do I need?
sentences.zh: 我需要什么？

sentences.en: That, that really is such a snapshot of that deeper gap within myself.
sentences.zh: 这，这真的是我内心深处那种巨大鸿沟的写照。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Did you open up Instagram and look?
sentences.zh: 你当时打开Instagram看了吗？

sentences.en: Like, how did you, what, what color towels did you leave with?
sentences.zh: 比如，你是怎么……你最后买了几号颜色的毛巾？

sentences.en: I want to say blue because probably it was, it's, it's America's favorite color.
sentences.zh: 我想说是蓝色，因为可能它是……这是美国人最喜欢的颜色。

sentences.en: They say it was probably the most agreeable color.
sentences.zh: 他们说这可能是最讨人喜欢的颜色。

sentences.en: It was the color that was fawning.
sentences.zh: 这是一种带着迎合色彩的颜色。

sentences.en: It was complimenting.
sentences.zh: 它在迎合别人。

sentences.en: It was a safe color.
sentences.zh: 它是一种安全的颜色。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Whereas now I really, I've, I, I love green.
sentences.zh: 然而现在我真的很……我，我爱绿色。

sentences.en: I love brown.
sentences.zh: 我爱棕色。

sentences.en: My favorite.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的。

sentences.en: Wait, I was going to say if Meg of now were in those aisles of Bed Bath & Beyond, what color towels are you going for?
sentences.zh: 等等，我本来想说，如果现在的梅格走在家居乐的过道里，你会挑什么颜色的毛巾？

sentences.en: Oh, definitely like an olive green or maybe a lighter green.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是橄榄绿或者浅绿色之类的。

sentences.en: I just love all greens.
sentences.zh: 我就是喜欢所有的绿色。

sentences.en: So soothing.
sentences.zh: 太舒缓了。

sentences.en: I've gotten so clear on my sense of style and what I like.
sentences.zh: 我对自己的审美品味以及自己喜欢什么已经非常明确了。

sentences.en: And I actually feel I have a very now specific preference.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实觉得自己现在有了非常具体的偏好。

sentences.en: And that's, that's a really cool sort of comparison.
sentences.zh: 这真是一种非常酷的对比。

sentences.en: I think it's a really striking question, a really striking scene.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个非常震撼的问题，一个非常震撼的场景。

sentences.en: What is my favorite color?
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的颜色是什么？

sentences.en: You're like genuinely asking yourself.
sentences.zh: 你就像是在真诚地质问自己。

sentences.en: And behind that question, of course, is not just a question of color.
sentences.zh: 当然，在这个问题背后，不仅仅是关于颜色的问题。

sentences.en: It's like, who am I, right?
sentences.zh: 就像是在问，我是谁，对吧？

sentences.en: Have I lost myself?
sentences.zh: 我是不是迷失了自我？

sentences.en: After you had that realization, what did you do with it?
sentences.zh: 当你有了这种觉悟之后，你用它做了什么？

sentences.en: What were the next steps you took?
sentences.zh: 你接下来采取了什么步骤？

sentences.en: Or was it a, was it years until you sort of began the work to figure out who you, who you were?
sentences.zh: 还是说，过了好几年你才开始努力弄清楚你是谁、你到底是谁？

sentences.en: That was definitely the beginning of what would be lots of deep processing to come.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一系列深层心理处理的开端。

sentences.en: But I always say healing starts with awareness and, you know, we really can't heal anything until we're aware of it.
sentences.zh: 但我总是说疗愈始于觉察，你知道的，在我们意识到问题之前，我们真的无法疗愈任何东西。

sentences.en: So that graduating college being on my own was really the, the beginning of having my survival patterns that did really keep me safe.
sentences.zh: 所以大学毕业并开始独立生活，真的是那些曾经真正保护过我的生存模式的起点。

sentences.en: If I'm now out of that context.
sentences.zh: 如果我现在已经脱离了那种环境。

sentences.en: And so now I'm just looking at them and they're, they're not fitting anymore,
sentences.zh: 所以现在我只是看着它们，它们不再合身了，

sentences.en: but I'm seeing them so much more clearly because I'm seeing these anxious patterns and it manifesting in my body.
sentences.zh: 但我把它们看得更清楚了，因为我看到了这些焦虑的模式以及它在我身体上的表现。

sentences.en: And, but not really having a quote reason to be feeling that way anymore.
sentences.zh: 而且，其实已经没有所谓的“理由”再让我有那种感觉了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I was still in relationship to my parents, but I wasn't living in that environment.
sentences.zh: 我依然和父母保持着联系，但我没有生活在那种环境中。

sentences.en: You know, you keep mentioning or connecting these patterns in your adult life to your experience growing up.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你一直把成年生活中的这些模式与你成长的经历联系起来。

sentences.en: And I wonder, like, as you began this sort of ongoing work of figuring out what you were doing and why, where were you tracing these behaviors back to?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，当开始着手弄清楚自己在做什么以及原因时，你把这些行为追溯到了哪里？

sentences.en: Like, tell me more about you as a kid and, and how you grew up, you know, reflecting on parental relationships is so complicated because there's nuance.
sentences.zh: 比如，跟我多讲讲你小时候的事，以及你是怎么长大的，反思父母关系是如此复杂，因为其中包含着微妙的情感。

sentences.en: We have so many moments with our caregivers or caregiver, depending on your home.
sentences.zh: 我们和抚养者（或者根据你的家庭情况，是某一位抚养者）有过很多这样的时刻。

sentences.en: And I talk about this of the complexity of, I, I thought it had to be all bad all the time in order for it to impact me.
sentences.zh: 我谈到过这种复杂性，我曾以为事情必须一直彻头彻尾地糟糕，才会对我产生影响。

sentences.en: And it wasn't, I felt like my dad kind of had to, I view as a child, I even had this visual.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此，我觉得我父亲某种程度上不得不……我小时候甚至有这样一个画面。

sentences.en: There were two of him.
sentences.zh: 他仿佛有两个分身。

sentences.en: You write about that in your book.
sentences.zh: 你在书中写到了这一点。

sentences.en: I was going to ask you about that.
sentences.zh: 我正想问你这个。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I was like, he was growing up and I think we hold this fantasy of our parents.
sentences.zh: 我就觉得，他是在成长，而我认为我们对父母抱有一种幻想。

sentences.en: And so while I was seeing him through this fantasy lens, he was my best friend and we had so much, we're so similar and we were both really like creative and impulsive and like,
sentences.zh: 所以，当透过这种幻想的镜头看他时，他是我的最好朋友，我们有那么多共同点，我们如此相似，我们都很有创造力、很冲动，而且，

sentences.en: we're just always, you know, spitball ideas to each other.
sentences.zh: 我们总是，你知道的，向彼此迸发各种想法。

sentences.en: That was so fun.
sentences.zh: 那真的很有趣。

sentences.en: And he was so hilarious.
sentences.zh: 而且他非常风趣。

sentences.en: But then he would switch into this other person that was rageful and really mean and critical and to my mom and to me, I became sort of the primary target as I became a teenager.
sentences.zh: 但随后他会变成另一个人，一个暴躁、非常刻薄和苛刻的人，对我妈妈如此，对我也是如此，当我成为青少年时，我某种程度上成了他的主要攻击目标。

sentences.en: And I think that's in part because I was starting to stand up for my mom.
sentences.zh: 我想部分原因是因为我开始站出来保护我妈妈。

sentences.en: And I remember wishing, I wish he was all bad so that I could just decide how I feel.
sentences.zh: 我记得我当时曾希望，我希望他彻头彻尾地变坏，这样我就可以直接决定自己的感受了。

sentences.en: It was so confusing for him to be both of these people at once.
sentences.zh: 他同时表现出这两种截然不同的人格，这让我感到非常困惑。

sentences.en: And yeah, we would have these big blowups.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们经常会有这样激烈的争吵。

sentences.en: And I remember I would just like have, you know, be in my room crying and hoping that he would knock on my door and apologize or acknowledge what happened.
sentences.zh: 我记得我当时会，你知道的，独自在房间里哭泣，希望他会来敲我的门并向我道歉，或者承认发生了什么。

sentences.en: And this is a really big dynamic that's important of when conflict is brushed under the rug, a parent doesn't take accountability.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要且关键的动态：当冲突被掩盖、父母不愿承担责任时，

sentences.en: There's no repair.
sentences.zh: 根本没有修复可言。

sentences.en: That is so damaging because the child, the only way the child can make sense of it is by believing they caused it to happen.
sentences.zh: 这极具破坏性，因为对于孩子来说，他们理解这一情况的唯一方法就是相信这一切是他们自己造成的。

sentences.en: And so they go from, I did something bad to make dad upset.
sentences.zh: 于是他们的想法从“我做错了事惹爸爸生气了”，

sentences.en: When that happens again and again and again, it forms the belief of, I am bad.
sentences.zh: 演变成了一次又一次发生这种情况后形成的信念：“我很坏。”

sentences.en: I must be so bad to make my parents so unhappy.
sentences.zh: “我一定很坏，才会让父母这么不开心。”

sentences.en: And this isn't to say, and I really want to make this clear because I don't want it to seem like, oh gosh, parents need to be perfect or whatever.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说——我真的很想把这点说清楚，因为我不想让人觉得，天哪，父母必须是完美的之类的。

sentences.en: There's no perfect parent.
sentences.zh: 世上没有完美的父母。

sentences.en: There's no perfect anyone.
sentences.zh: 世上没有完美的人。

sentences.en: And we're going to, it's, conflict is inevitable and it's good.
sentences.zh: 我们会……冲突是不可避免的，而且冲突是件好事。

sentences.en: Like it's, it's friction.
sentences.zh: 就像它是一种摩擦力。

sentences.en: Repair is the most important thing.
sentences.zh: 修复才是最重要的事情。

sentences.en: If a parent yells, of course, how could you, like we all have our moments.
sentences.zh: 如果父母吼了孩子，当然，怎么会……我们所有人都有情绪失控的时候。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But to, after the fact say, hey, I'm really sorry for yelling at you.
sentences.zh: 但在事后说：“嘿，我对刚才对你大吼大叫感到非常抱歉。”

sentences.en: That was on me.
sentences.zh: “那是我的问题。”

sentences.en: That wasn't your fault.
sentences.zh: “那不是你的错。”

sentences.en: I'm really working on managing my emotions and I'm going to, I'm going to try better next time.
sentences.zh: “我正在努力控制自己的情绪，下次我会做得更好。”

sentences.en: And I love you and I'm here.
sentences.zh: “我爱你，我一直在。”

sentences.en: That is so healing for a child or anyone to hear.
sentences.zh: 对于一个孩子或任何人来说，听到这些是极具疗愈效果的。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about, you say, the only way a child can make sense of it is to believe that they caused it.
sentences.zh: 我联想到，正如你所说，孩子理解这一情况的唯一方法就是相信是自己造成了这一切。

sentences.en: And that speaks, that connects to me, to the shame we sort of opened this conversation about.
sentences.zh: 这与我们这次对话开头时谈到的羞耻感产生了共鸣。

sentences.en: I am inherently bad.
sentences.zh: 我生来就是坏的。

sentences.en: And maybe when you're feeling that way, you know, you're 31, having anxiety because you were too loud at the function.
sentences.zh: 也许当你怀有这种感受时，你已经31岁了，却因为在聚会中表现得太吵闹而感到焦虑。

sentences.en: And that's at the core of it.
sentences.zh: 而这正是核心所在。

sentences.en: It's like, I can't trace that back to childhood, for example, but sort of that is the thread that's connecting it.
sentences.zh: 比如，我无法把这直接追溯到童年，但这就是将它们连接在一起的纽带。

sentences.en: And was there a moment or a series of moments you tell me where you, where you started to put these pieces together and you realized like, oh,
sentences.zh: 有没有某个时刻或某系列时刻——你来告诉我——让你开始把这些拼图拼凑起来，并意识到，哦，

sentences.en: because of the life that I led as a child and a teen, this is why I'm reacting that way as an adult.
sentences.zh: 正因为我作为儿童和青少年时期的生活经历，我才会在成年后做出这样的反应？

sentences.en: Was there like a moment on your therapist's couch or like, was there an aha moment for you or was it, was it different than that?
sentences.zh: 有没有像是在治疗师的躺椅上的某个时刻，或者说有什么恍然大悟的时刻，还是说过程有所不同？

sentences.en: I would say there were a lot of moments, but it started with just an insufferable amount of anxiety in my body, in my mind that I felt in college.
sentences.zh: 我会说有很多这样的时刻，但这一切都始于我在大学期间感受到的、身体和脑海中那种难以忍受的焦虑。

sentences.en: And I actually met my husband in college.
sentences.zh: 我实际上是在大学里认识我丈夫的。

sentences.en: We were 19.
sentences.zh: 我们当时19岁。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Right off the bat, he was just such a safe, steady person, has never yelled at me, has never lied to me.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，他就是一个非常安全、稳重的人，从未对我吼过，从未对我说过谎。

sentences.en: And that was so wild.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: I noticed just so much fearful thinking around him where I knew my body, my intuition trusted that he was safe, but my thoughts were, he's going to flip, just wait,
sentences.zh: 我发现自己在面对他时，脑海中有着如此之多的恐惧思维：虽然我的身体和直觉相信他是安全的，但我的想法却是，他会翻脸的，等着瞧吧，

sentences.en: you're going to say the wrong thing and he's going to turn into someone that you don't know.
sentences.zh: 你只要说错一句话，他就会变成一个你根本不认识的人。

sentences.en: He'll, he'll get drunk and something horrible will happen or something, something like that.
sentences.zh: 他会喝醉，然后发生可怕的事情，或者类似的事情。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, it, it just felt, it felt quite, it felt quite confusing at that time, but you know, it's, I don't, I don't want to make it sound like there's this distinct, oh,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，在当时感觉……感觉相当困惑，但你知道的，我不想让你觉得，这里有一个截然分明的界限，哦，

sentences.en: I was in childhood and then I went to adulthood.
sentences.zh: 我经历过童年，然后我步入了成年。

sentences.en: And now I can see the clear because I actually, I'd say some of my most traumatic memories were actually from my twenties with my parents because that's where a lot of emotional,
sentences.zh: 现在我能看清一切了，因为实际上，我要说我的一些最具创伤的记忆其实来自于我二十多岁时与父母相处的日子，因为正是在那时，许多情感上的……

sentences.en: the emotional neglect started to happen, which I think is in part why I was drawn to the essay that we'll read today.
sentences.zh: 情感上的忽视开始出现，我想这也是为什么我会被我们今天将要阅读的那篇散文所吸引的部分原因。

sentences.en: But I don't want to, I don't want to, I don't want the distinction to be so sharp, but rather just to point to how this anxious thinking, this, are you mad at me thinking,
sentences.zh: 但我不想……我不想让这种界限变得如此鲜明，而是想指出这种焦虑的思维——这种“你生我的气吗”的思维、

sentences.en: am I in trouble thinking was helpful.
sentences.zh: “我惹上麻烦了吗”的思维——曾经是如何起到保护作用的。

sentences.en: And then it started to not feel so helpful when I was no longer in that environment.
sentences.zh: 而当我不再处于那种环境中时，它就开始变得不再那么有用了。

sentences.en: I really appreciate what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 我很感激你所说的话。

sentences.en: It's like so much work can happen.
sentences.zh: 这就像是可以通过生活在感觉良好的关系中，来完成大量的自我建设。

sentences.en: So much healing can happen by just living in relationships that feel good.
sentences.zh: 大量的疗愈可以通过生活在感觉良好的关系中发生。

sentences.en: And two, to recognize the things that we, that we carry, right, from early relationships in your case, you know, from the way you were raised from your childhood.
sentences.zh: 其次，是要认识到我们所承载的东西，对吧？那些来自早期关系的负荷，在你的例子中，你知道的，来自于你的成长方式和你的童年。

sentences.en: This idea of like a sort of legacy, like I said, the things we carry from our early relationships, it's reminding me a lot of the Modern Love essay you chose to read today.
sentences.zh: 这种类似于某种精神遗产的概念——就像我说的，我们从早期关系中承载的东西——这让我想起了你今天选择阅读的那篇《现代爱情》专栏散文。

sentences.en: This is an essay about our complex relationships with parents, our own, other people's.
sentences.zh: 这是一篇关于我们与父母之间复杂关系的散文，包括我们自己的父母以及别人的父母。

sentences.en: It's called My Three Years as a Beloved Daughter by Erin Brown.
sentences.zh: 它由艾琳·布朗（Erin Brown）撰写，题目是《我作为被珍爱女儿的三年》。

sentences.en: Can you speak a little bit about why you were drawn to this essay and why you chose it?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈为什么会被这篇散文吸引、为什么选择它吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: This essay is so, so sharply speaks to a feeling of, oh, grief for what we don't have and longing, envy, seeing other people have what we want in a relationship.
sentences.zh: 这篇散文非常、非常深刻地道出了一种感觉：哦，为我们所没有的东西感到悲伤和渴望、艳羡，看到别人在亲密关系中拥有我们想要的东西。

sentences.en: But I was also drawn to the essay because my dad actually passed away in January, which is two days after I turned in the final manuscripts for the book,
sentences.zh: 但我也被这篇散文吸引，因为我父亲实际上是在一月份去世的，那是我的书提交最终稿的两天后，

sentences.en: which was so confusing because I grieved the hope that he would change.
sentences.zh: 这让人感到非常困惑，因为我曾为他会改变的希望而悲伤。

sentences.en: And I think that comes through in the essay a lot, hope that if I'm, if I'm just, and this is the fond response, hard at work, if I'm just better, if I'm just good enough,
sentences.zh: 我想这在散文中体现得很明显：那种希望——如果我只是……这就是迎合反应，在拼命努力——如果我只是更好一点，如果我足够优秀，

sentences.en: if I just achieve enough, if I'm just easy enough and pleasant enough, he'll like me more.
sentences.zh: 如果我取得的成就足够多，如果我足够省事、足够讨人喜欢，他就会更喜欢我。

sentences.en: And grieving that, you know, his reactivity is nothing to do with me.
sentences.zh: 而为之悲伤的是，你知道的，他的反复无常与我毫无关系。

sentences.en: And it's, I, I can't, I can't fix him.
sentences.zh: 而且，我……我无法改变他。

sentences.en: I can't change him.
sentences.zh: 我改变不了他。

sentences.en: This is the extent of what he can give me in this lifetime.
sentences.zh: 这就是他在今生所能给我的全部极限了。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: This essay encapsulates a certain, like a longing for our parents to be different or for the, for the, the, the author has this,
sentences.zh: 这篇文章蕴含着某种渴望，比如渴望我们的父母能有所不同，或者渴望……作者有这样一种，

sentences.en: this hope that maybe her parents will give her something she was missing.
sentences.zh: 这种希望，也许她的父母会给她一些她所缺失的东西。

sentences.en: And it sounds like you're saying you resonate with that, that longing, that hope.
sentences.zh: 听起来你是在说，你对那种渴望、那种希望深有共鸣。

sentences.en: Gosh.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So much, so much, this longing of, I mean, I remember having this feeling as a child, I would go home, I'd be at home for Christmas or whatever.
sentences.zh: 真的好强烈，这种渴望……我的意思是，我记得自己小时候就有这种感觉，我会回家，回家过圣诞节什么的。

sentences.en: And having this feeling of, I want to go home.
sentences.zh: 然后就会有这种感觉：我想回家。

sentences.en: You'd be at home and you'd.
sentences.zh: 你明明在家，然后你……

sentences.en: I'm at home and I'm feeling like I want to go home.
sentences.zh: 我在家里，却感觉我想回家。

sentences.en: Like it's not, it's not, this isn't it.
sentences.zh: 就好像这不是、不是，这不是那种感觉。

sentences.en: Um, so yeah, that longing is so strong and I don't think we have in our society, a lot of words for it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以那种渴望是如此强烈，而且我觉得我们的社会里并没有太多词汇来形容它。

sentences.en: I think we talk a lot about grief when someone has passed, but I don't think we talk about this type of grief of grieving what we don't have, grieving what we'll never be as much.
sentences.zh: 我觉得当有人离世时我们会谈论很多悲伤，但我觉得我们很少谈论这种悲伤——为我们没有的东西而悲伤，为我们永远无法成为的样子而悲伤。

sentences.en: When we come back, Meg Josephson reads the essay, My Three Years as a Beloved Daughter by Erin Brown.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，梅格·约瑟夫森（Meg Josephson）将朗读埃琳·布朗（Erin Brown）的文章《我做被爱女儿的三年》。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘（Wynna Liu）。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《纽约时报》游戏部的字谜游戏《连线》。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基（Sam Azersky），我每天负责制作《拼字蜂》和《字母箱》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像刚才你听到声音的这些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games，今天就开始游玩。

sentences.en: My Three Years as a Beloved Daughter by Erin Brown
sentences.zh: 《我做被爱女儿的三年》，作者埃琳·布朗

sentences.en: When I turned 29, my parents called from Boise with birthday wishes, but they soon moved on to how the wildfires in Idaho were the worst they had seen in years.
sentences.zh: 在我29岁生日那天，远在博伊西的父母打来电话祝我生日快乐，但他们很快就把话题转到了爱达荷州的野火上，说那是他们多年来见过最严重的一次。

sentences.en: Their voices were somehow softer for the distance, and I knew they had more pressing things on their mind than their grown daughter's birthday.
sentences.zh: 由于距离的原因，他们的声音听起来不知为何柔和了一些，我明白比起成年女儿的生日，他们心里有更紧急的事。

sentences.en: With the lonesome click of the telephone behind me, I thought about my other family, and the parents who wouldn't be calling.
sentences.zh: 伴随着电话挂断时那孤独的咔哒声，我想到了我的另一个家庭，以及那些不会打来电话的父母。

sentences.en: The parents who believed that no daughter is ever too old for a birthday party, for the cake, and the tiara.
sentences.zh: 那些认为没有哪个女儿会嫌过生日、吃蛋糕、戴皇冠太老的父母。

sentences.en: For three years, while I was living in New York, my best friend's parents loved me.
sentences.zh: 整整三年，当我住在纽约时，我最好朋友的父母爱着我。

sentences.en: They loved me because of how much they loved their daughter, a devotion I witnessed at Thanksgiving, Easter, graduation dinners, and birthdays.
sentences.zh: 他们爱我是因为他们极其爱自己的女儿，这种深情我在感恩节、复活节、毕业晚宴和生日会上都见证过。

sentences.en: Those occasions when I left the city with my friend to visit them.
sentences.zh: 每逢那些时刻，我都会和朋友一起离开城市去拜访他们。

sentences.en: There was even one year when I was stuck in the city with a Christmas Eve bartending shift.
sentences.zh: 甚至有一年，我被困在城里值圣诞夜的酒保班。

sentences.en: The next day, feeling urban and weathered and brave, I boarded the Metro-North commuter train at Grand Central Terminal and headed to Westport, Connecticut,
sentences.zh: 第二天，我带着一种饱经城市风霜又勇敢无畏的感觉，在大中央车站登上了大都会北方铁路的通勤列车，前往康涅狄格州的韦斯特波特，

sentences.en: to the home that felt as if it were almost mine.
sentences.zh: 去那个感觉仿佛几乎属于我的家。

sentences.en: I had packed a tote accordingly, and had filled it with a small batch of wrapped gifts.
sentences.zh: 我相应地打包了一个托特包，里面塞满了精心打包的小礼物。

sentences.en: A photo frame from a boutique in Park Slope, Brooklyn, books by Barbara Ehrenreich and Paul Bowles, silver earrings from the holiday market at Bryant Park in Manhattan,
sentences.zh: 一个来自布鲁克林公园坡精品店的照片框，芭芭拉·埃伦赖希和保罗·鲍尔斯的书，曼哈顿布莱恩特公园假日集市的银耳环，

sentences.en: and a bottle of wine.
sentences.zh: 以及一瓶酒。

sentences.en: I knew they would tell me it was too much, that I shouldn't have, really, but I knew also that they would have gifts for me.
sentences.zh: 我知道他们会告诉我说这太贵重了，真的不用破费，但我也知道他们也会为我准备礼物。

sentences.en: And besides, I was grateful for the invitation, grateful to be enveloped yet again in the heavy quilt of this family's love.
sentences.zh: 再说，我很感激能受到邀请，感激再次被这个家庭浓浓的爱意紧紧包裹。

sentences.en: And they loved their daughter.
sentences.zh: 他们爱他们的女儿。

sentences.en: They love her.
sentences.zh: 他们爱她。

sentences.en: In trying to explain the appeal of their relationship to my other friends, I would find myself at a loss.
sentences.zh: 当我试图向其他朋友解释他们这种关系的魅力时，我发现自己词穷了。

sentences.en: As if I had been asked to capture in a few words the wonders of the Grand Canyon or the Costa Rican rainforests.
sentences.zh: 就像有人让我用寥寥数语捕捉大峡谷或哥斯达黎加雨林的奇景一样。

sentences.en: You don't understand, I would say, widening my eyes and shaking my head.
sentences.zh: 你们不明白，我会睁大眼睛、摇着头说。

sentences.en: They just love her.
sentences.zh: 他们就是好爱她。

sentences.en: Theirs was a family of abundance.
sentences.zh: 这是一个丰盈的家庭。

sentences.en: Of love, intellect, ambition, food.
sentences.zh: 充满了爱、才智、雄心和食物。

sentences.en: Shrimp cocktail, Cosmos and long-stemmed martini glasses, goat cheese with cranberries, sirloin, apricots dipped in chocolate, margaritas, wine, port.
sentences.zh: 鲜虾鸡尾酒、大都会鸡尾酒和长脚马提尼杯、带蔓越莓的山羊奶酪、西冷牛排、裹着巧克力的杏子、玛格丽特、葡萄酒、波特酒。

sentences.en: I would eat until my eyes glassed over.
sentences.zh: 我会吃到眼睛发直。

sentences.en: I was sure that even my own wedding would not compare to the luxury of eating a holiday meal with my East Coast family.
sentences.zh: 我确信，即使是我自己的婚礼，也比不上和东海岸家人一起享用节日大餐那般奢华。

sentences.en: Pleasure was always a main course at their table, and I hungrily devoured their effortless enjoyment of one another.
sentences.zh: 快乐永远是他们餐桌上的主菜，我如饥似渴地贪恋着他们之间那种毫不费力的融洽。

sentences.en: There was an intense loyalty in this family that I had not encountered before.
sentences.zh: 这个家庭有一种我从未见过的强烈忠诚。

sentences.en: I assumed it must have something to do with vacations in Hawaii, carpooling to soccer games, all the things that my childhood lacked.
sentences.zh: 我猜这一定和夏威夷度假、拼车去踢足球有关，这些都是我的童年所缺乏的。

sentences.en: My best friend's father took great interest in her career.
sentences.zh: 我最好朋友的父亲对她的职业表现出极大的兴趣。

sentences.en: Whenever she talked about her struggles at the office, he listened attentively, inevitably taking her side.
sentences.zh: 每当她谈起在职场上的挣扎，他总是聚精会神地听着，并且不可避免地站在她这一边。

sentences.en: We could see the blood rise and worry that he would make calls on her behalf.
sentences.zh: 我们能看到他青筋暴起，并担心他会亲自出面替她出头。

sentences.en: Her mother was less direct.
sentences.zh: 她的母亲则没有那么直接。

sentences.en: She merely sat Shiva for every person who wronged her children, not out of mourning, but as a ceremonial acknowledgement of the fact that the person had ceased to exiSt.
sentences.zh: 她只是为每一个对不起她孩子的恶人进行了一场“坐期谷”（犹太丧葬习俗），倒不是为了哀悼，而是作为一种仪式，宣告这个人已经不复存在的事实。

sentences.en: It didn't matter that she was a staunch Episcopalian.
sentences.zh: 她是不是坚定的圣公会信徒并不重要。

sentences.en: Dead to me, she would say whenever the name of an ex-boyfriend came up in conversation.
sentences.zh: “对我来说已经死了，”每当对话中提起某个前男友的名字时，她总是会这么说。

sentences.en: I don't even know that name.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道那个名字。

sentences.en: I secretly wished for an ex-boyfriend worthy of her ire.
sentences.zh: 我暗自希望能有一个配得上她这种怒火的前男友。

sentences.en: In every family, there are certain roles to be filled, and my role was to offer a kind of self-deprecating comic relief.
sentences.zh: 在每个家庭里，都有需要扮演的特定角色，而我的角色就是提供一种自嘲式的喜剧调剂。

sentences.en: I entertained the tables with stories from the Peace Corps in which I was the star,
sentences.zh: 我在饭桌上讲着我在和平队里担任主角的故事来逗大家开心，

sentences.en: and during which I often found myself flapping my arms around or pointing ridiculously at my own head.
sentences.zh: 在那期间，我经常手舞足蹈，或者滑稽地指着自己的脑袋。

sentences.en: And bless them, they laughed.
sentences.zh: 承蒙他们不弃，他们都笑了。

sentences.en: I am sure that my desperate need to be adored, my clinging vulnerability, was not lost on my friend's parents.
sentences.zh: 我确信，我那种对被崇拜的绝望需求、那种患得患失的脆弱感，并没有逃过我朋友父母的眼睛。

sentences.en: I had jokes from Africa.
sentences.zh: 我有来自非洲的笑话。

sentences.en: I had jokes from the bar.
sentences.zh: 我有来自酒吧的笑话。

sentences.en: And they laughed and loved me for it.
sentences.zh: 他们笑了，并为此而爱我。

sentences.en: They loved the fact that I was a bartender, possibly because it meant that their own daughter was not.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢我是一名酒保，可能是因为这意味着他们自己的女儿不是。

sentences.en: Make no mistake.
sentences.zh: 别误会。

sentences.en: My own parents loved me.
sentences.zh: 我的父母其实是爱我的。

sentences.en: It's just that their love was manifested in ways that I began to see as indicative of an east-west divide.
sentences.zh: 只不过他们的爱表现出的方式，让我开始觉得那是东西部差异的象征。

sentences.en: When I left home, it was as if my parents had sent me off in a covered wagon to claim my own plot of land in the valley.
sentences.zh: 当我离开家时，就好像父母把我送上了一辆篷车，让我去山谷里开拓属于自己的一片土地。

sentences.en: Everything I needed, they assumed, was already in the wagon.
sentences.zh: 他们认为我需要的一切，都已经装在车上了。

sentences.en: They respected my autonomy, thought that bartending was an adventure almost as worthwhile as the Peace Corps,
sentences.zh: 他们尊重我的独立性，认为当酒保是一场几乎和加入和平队一样有价值的冒险，

sentences.en: and believed that it was better to be mildly poor with an abundance of vacation time and the promise of great things than to be gainfully employed and disappointed.
sentences.zh: 并且坚信与其有一份报酬丰厚但充满失望的工作，倒不如既有大把假期、前途充满希望，又稍微过得清贫一点。

sentences.en: They sent money to fill occasional holes in my budget, but they didn't lavish me with gifts and praise, and they didn't worry about me.
sentences.zh: 他们会寄钱来填补我偶尔的财务空洞，但他们不会用礼物和赞美对我进行狂轰滥炸，他们也不为我操心。

sentences.en: The time for worry had passed.
sentences.zh: 操心的年纪已经过去了。

sentences.en: My independence was something I had fought for throughout high school.
sentences.zh: 我的独立是我在整个高中时期一直在争取的东西。

sentences.en: Having finally won it by the twin defaults of age and distance, I was uneasy with my parents' quiet faith in my abilities.
sentences.zh: 既然通过年龄和距离这两个默认条件终于赢得了独立，我对父母那种对我能力的静静信任反而感到有些不安。

sentences.en: My East Coast family's love was tangible.
sentences.zh: 我东海岸家庭的爱是切实可感的。

sentences.en: It was fine wine and heavy cream, knitted scarves and photo albuMs.
sentences.zh: 那是上等的美酒和浓奶油，针织围巾和相册。

sentences.en: I envied the concern and adulation that they bestowed upon their daughter.
sentences.zh: 我嫉妒他们倾注在女儿身上的关怀与奉承。

sentences.en: I wanted some for myself.
sentences.zh: 我也想为自己争取一些。

sentences.en: When I got into graduate school, I called my family in the West, but my East Coast family called me.
sentences.zh: 当我考上研究生时，我给西部的家人打了电话，但东海岸的家人却主动打电话给我。

sentences.en: They were so proud, and said it.
sentences.zh: 他们太骄傲了，并且大声说出来。

sentences.en: Were so proud.
sentences.zh: 真的太骄傲了。

sentences.en: I thought I might remain a member of my East Coast family forever.
sentences.zh: 我以为我可能会永远成为东海岸家庭的一员。

sentences.en: But families often split up, even the most attractive ones.
sentences.zh: 但家庭往往会破裂，即使是最迷人的家庭也是如此。

sentences.en: And mine was no different.
sentences.zh: 我的家庭也不例外。

sentences.en: My best friend and I had often joked about the conflicting patterns of our personalities,
sentences.zh: 我和我最好的朋友经常拿我们彼此冲突的性格特点开玩笑，

sentences.en: as though the differences between us excused the friendship from the trivial spats that other friends routinely endured.
sentences.zh: 就好像我们之间的差异让这段友谊免于其他朋友经常忍受的那些琐碎争吵。

sentences.en: Perhaps we knew all along that there could never be a small fight between us.
sentences.zh: 也许我们从一开始就知道，我们之间绝不会发生小争吵。

sentences.en: Only a big one.
sentences.zh: 只会是大吵一架。

sentences.en: And eventually, it happened.
sentences.zh: 最终，事情还是发生了。

sentences.en: We had our big fight.
sentences.zh: 我们爆发了一场大争吵。

sentences.en: We argued ourselves up to the stubborn wall of apology, and neither of us could scale it.
sentences.zh: 我们争吵着，直到碰壁在“道歉”这堵顽固的墙前，谁也无法翻越过去。

sentences.en: I think it surprised both of us how tenuous our friendship really was.
sentences.zh: 我想我们俩都很惊讶，我们的友谊原来如此脆弱。

sentences.en: Bitter words.
sentences.zh: 尖酸刻薄的话语。

sentences.en: All the hurt that a too-close relationship can nurture.
sentences.zh: 过于亲密的关系所能滋生的所有伤害。

sentences.en: Phones turned off.
sentences.zh: 手机关机。

sentences.en: And just like that, three months passed.
sentences.zh: 就这样，三个月过去了。

sentences.en: Thanksgiving came and went with no word from my friend or her parents.
sentences.zh: 感恩节来了又去，我和朋友以及她的父母再无任何联系。

sentences.en: Stranded on the East Coast, I was host to my own dinner and invited all the wayward souls I knew.
sentences.zh: 滞留在东海岸的我独自办了晚餐会，邀请了我认识的所有孤独无依的灵魂。

sentences.en: I pretended not to wait for my phone to ring, though I carried it in the pocket of my apron, as I mistakenly prepared enough mashed potatoes for all the urchins in a Dickens novel.
sentences.zh: 我假装不在乎手机有没有响，虽然把它揣在围裙口袋里，同时愚蠢地准备了足够多狄更斯小说里所有流浪儿吃的土豆泥。

sentences.en: But Christmas.
sentences.zh: 但是圣诞节。

sentences.en: Surely I would hear from them at Christmas.
sentences.zh: 到了圣诞节我总该听到他们的消息吧。

sentences.en: I knew my friend would not call, but probably never call.
